title: Tulamani Patel v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Second writ dismissed as same cause of action.
headnote: The petitioner sought mandamus directing the distribution licensee to decide representations dated 26 March 2021 and 7 July 2021 on a disputed electricity bill. In Writ-C No. 386 of 2020 the Court had already declined to quash the recovery citation and relegated the billing-correctness dispute to clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Treating the present petition as a second writ on the same cause of action, the Division Bench dismissed it.
facts: Tulamani Patel had earlier filed Writ-C No. 386 of 2020 seeking to quash a recovery citation dated 9 December 2019, disputing the correctness of his electricity bill. That petition was disposed of by relegating him to clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a two-week window to approach the authority and short-term protection against coercive recovery. He thereafter made representations dated 26 March 2021 and 7 July 2021. In this writ he sought mandamus directing respondent no. 2 to decide those representations within a court-fixed period.

holding_units.holding: Where a consumer disputing bill correctness has already been relegated to the statutory remedy under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, a later writ seeking mandamus to decide the resulting representations is a second writ on the same cause of action and is dismissed.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated mandamus to decide the 26 March 2021 and 7 July 2021 representations as a second writ on the same billing dispute that Writ-C No. 386 of 2020 had already sent to clause 6.5, and dismissed it.
The quoted earlier order, which this Bench applied, had held that a dispute as to correctness of the bill is to be pursued under clause 6.5 and is not to be entertained in writ.

not_decided.point: correctness of the electricity bill and the pending 6.5 representations
not_decided.note: The Court dismissed the second writ without examining the bill or directing decision of the representations dated 26 March 2021 and 7 July 2021.
